rv.q: Maria Telnikoff’s play is a story of same-sex parenting, with just enough charm to cover up its unevenness.
This is an enjoyable show that resolves easily enough as people see the good intentions of others in this situation.
This is a production with real promise, well worth seeing as it continues to develop.
The plot feels confused, with timelines that don’t quite make sense and scenarios that wouldn’t happen in real life.

cn.t: This rom-com about same-sex parenting and modern friendship garners mixed reviews. Critics find charm in the ensemble chemistry and timely premise, but note uneven execution across its brisk 90 minutes.
